Subject: Re: Fwd: Unusual latency/errors on prediction endpoints

Status update from runtime triage: between 07:45-08:00 we observed a sudden cluster-wide shard rebalancing event triggered by a preemptible-host reclamation in the primary AZ. The scheduler attempted to drain several GPU instances simultaneously which caused transient capacity shortfall. Because FinSuite’s requests are pinned to our Dedicated pool (and they have committed throughput), the fallback routing rules were not aggressive enough to spill to compatible hosted model variants — current fallback threshold is 40% utilization and we hit ~88% for sustained windows.

Immediate technical mitigations applied (10:00):
- Emergency cross-AZ spill enabled for FinSuite traffic (non-blocking routing to a compatible quantized variant in a spare pool).
- Increased KV cache affinity timeout to reduce regen overhead.
- Short-term autoscale burst enabled for the affected Dedicated pool (manual override) for 2 hours.

Observed effects: error rate down from 3.8% to 0.9% and p99 improved to ~520ms after spill. Not fully back to baseline. We suspect two contributing gaps: (1) our reserved capacity admission logic allowed commitments that sum above practical physical slack in the pool during simultaneous reclaim events; (2) fallback routing policy thresholds are too conservative for reserved customers.

I’m recommending an exec decision on whether we: (A) immediately shift more capacity to FinSuite (impacting other tenants' latency for up to 30m), or (B) honor strict isolation and offer larger financial remediation + guaranteed timeline for full restore.

— Marcus
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

Subject: Executive summary + decision log (pool surge, reserved shortfall)

Team —
Summary for execs and next actions (for VP/CTO review):
- Incident: 2026-10-05 07:45 PDT — cluster rebalancing due to preemptible host reclamation caused sustained utilization spike (peak ~88%) in the Dedicated pool serving FinSuite. Resulted in elevated p99 and 5xxs for a high-value customer.
- Immediate remediation: cross-AZ spill + manual autoscale burst reduced errors to ~0.9% and p99 to ~520ms. Customer reports improvement but not full baseline.
- Root causes identified: (1) admission and headroom assumptions for aggregate reserved commitments are overly optimistic for simultaneous AZ reclamation; (2) fallback routing thresholds for reserved customers are too conservative; (3) insufficient telemetries to predict reclaim risk windows.

Decision requested: choose one of the following by EOD today
1) Prioritize customer experience: reallocate reserved spare capacity to FinSuite for up to 60 minutes (impact other tenants; will require exec sign-off) — we will log the decision and apply compensating credits to affected tenants.
2) Preserve isolation: maintain isolation and offer FinSuite a formal remediation package (30% usage credit today + commitment to architecture fixes in 30 days).

Proposed permanent fixes (30/60/90 day plan)
- 30d: Lower fallback threshold for reserved customers and add rapid-spill policy.
- 60d: Admission control sanity checks factoring in cross-AZ reclaim risk and preemptible-host schedules.
- 90d: New telemetry and predictivity signal for reclaim likelihood and pre-emptive autoscale triggers.

Jira: INFRA-4337 (engineering remediation). HubSpot: DEAL-7891 (customer remediation path). Attached: throughput logs and proposed mutual action plan v2.

If no exec reply by EOD, we will proceed with option (1) for a 30 minute protection window to prevent further customer impact. Please reply with your choice and any objections.

— Soojin
